Small-multiple dot map, one panel per pathway

Source: R/pathway_small_multiples_map.R
mysterymaps_pathway_small_multiples_map.Rd

Facets a physician dot map by a grouping column – typically a certification or training pathway – so each pathway's geographic footprint is visible on its own panel instead of overplotted in one colour-coded map. Optionally adds a combined "All Pathways Combined" panel first, for a baseline readers can compare the per-pathway panels against.

Usage

mysterymaps_pathway_small_multiples_map(
  points,
  basemap,
  pathway_var,
  pathway_labels = NULL,
  include_combined_panel = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  point_size = 1.6,
  point_alpha = 0.9,
  crs = 5070,
  jitter_miles = 1.5,
  jitter_seed = 42,
  ncol = NULL
)

Arguments

points

sf POINT layer, one row per physician.

basemap

sf polygon layer to draw beneath the points in every panel.

pathway_var

character(1): column in points identifying the pathway.

pathway_labels

Optional named character vector recoding raw pathway_var values to full-word facet and legend labels. NULL uses the raw values as-is.

include_combined_panel

logical(1): add an "All Pathways Combined" panel containing every point. Default TRUE.

title, subtitle, caption

Character labels. NULL omits.

palette

Optional named colour vector for pathway_var (after pathway_labels recoding), e.g. c("Urology" = "#009E73"). NULL uses a hue scale.

point_size, point_alpha

Point aesthetics.

crs

Projection for display. Default EPSG:5070 (Albers Equal Area), appropriate for the contiguous United States.

jitter_miles, jitter_seed

Passed to mysterymaps_jitter_points(). Defaults 1.5 and 42.

ncol

Number of facet columns. NULL lets ggplot2::facet_wrap() choose.

Value

A ggplot object. The caller saves it; this function writes nothing.

Details

pathway_var's raw values become the facet titles verbatim, which makes any abbreviation in the source data ("OBGYN", "ABU") land directly on the figure. Pass pathway_labels, a named character vector mapping raw values to full words (e.g. c(OBGYN = "Obstetrics and Gynecology", ABU = "Urology")), to recode them before faceting; this function does not expand abbreviations on its own.

Jitter uses mysterymaps_jitter_points() with the same deterministic, under-2-mile default as mysterymaps_physician_dot_map(), applied once before faceting so a physician's dot sits at the same jittered position in every panel it appears in.

Points are coloured by pathway (the same grouping that drives the facets), using ggplot2::scale_color_hue() unless palette is supplied. Every per-pathway panel is then visually uniform, as expected – but the "All Pathways Combined" panel keeps each point's own pathway colour rather than flattening to one colour, so it works as a real overview rather than a silhouette of the dataset.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
pts <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(lon = -99.5 + 0:7, lat = 40.2 + (0:7) * 0.2,
            pathway = rep(c("OBGYN", "URO"), length.out = 8)),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
basemap <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-100, -97, -97, -100, -100), c(39, 39, 42, 42, 39)))),
  crs = 4326))
mysterymaps_pathway_small_multiples_map(pts, basemap, pathway_var = "pathway")
}
